counterfactual_missing_items: Testicular ultrasound: No neoplasm identified (no testicular primary seen; extragonadal/retroperitoneal choriocarcinoma remains the best fit)
decisive_items: Initial serum β-hCG: 691 IU/L (normal 0-5 IU/L), increased to 1860 IU/L on repeat
Poorly differentiated tumor composed of syncytial, intermediate in situ trophoblastic cells
Immunostaining positive for AE1/AE3, CAM5.2, inhibin, β-hCG (strongly), Glypican-3 and PLAP (focally)
response.rationale: R1 directly integrates the strongly elevated and rising β-hCG, the trophoblastic histology, and the strongly positive β-hCG immunostaining, explaining both the hemorrhagic right adrenal mass and the pulmonary nodules. R3 is the closest alternative because it captures trophoblastic identity, but it does not commit to the specific choriocarcinoma subtype. R2 mistakenly treats the tumor hemorrhage as the primary diagnosis, R4 is a nonspecific metastatic-pattern label, and C1 simply reappends the R3 completion without adding the β-hCG-derived specificity.

rejected.why: Correlated restatement/completion of R3; the same trophoblastic span is already represented and it does not incorporate β-hCG specificity.
Adrenal hemorrhage is only the imaging appearance of the underlying trophoblastic tumor; it cannot explain elevated β-hCG or the trophoblastic pathology.
Nonspecific metastatic disease citing pulmonary nodules and family history; this does not account for the trophoblastic tumor, β-hCG elevation, or β-hCG immunostaining.
